_source: research/137-taxonomy-proposal.md section 3 (label set + forensic question + boundary rules), decision log section 4
_note: 20 core labels (fixed, multi-label, Unclassified mandatory) + 5 opt-in overlay labels never scored in core macro-F1.
_supervision_note: The `name`, `question` and `boundary` fields are copied verbatim from research/137-taxonomy-proposal.md section 3, which was written and frozen BEFORE the fixture was labelled and contains no instance drawn from the fixture. These three fields are the ONLY supervision the five model-backed candidates receive. Any change to them must be justified against the proposal, not against fixture performance.
_overlay_scoring: Overlay labels are OUT OF SCOPE for this bench run: no candidate emits them and the fixture carries no overlay gold rows. Declared explicitly here rather than left as a silent third state.

core.name: Search & Query
core.question: What did the subject look for, in their own words?
core.boundary: Applies to search-engine result pages and to in-site search endpoints. The subject of the query does not change this label; a query about a second topic is a second label under multi-label.

core.name: Webmail, Messaging & Voice
core.question: How were they communicating off-channel?
core.boundary: Web-hosted mail, chat, messaging and voice/meeting services. Message content is not visible in a history row; this label asserts the channel, never the conversation.

core.name: Social media & Online communities
core.question: What accounts and what contacts?
core.boundary: Social networks, forums, community platforms, professional networks, personal blogs, and dating/matchmaking services.

core.name: News & Current affairs
core.question: What was the subject reading about, and when relative to the incident?
core.boundary: Press, broadcast news, aggregators.

core.name: Reference, Education & How-to
core.question: Was the subject learning or researching a method?
core.boundary: Encyclopaedic and reference material, courses, academic and institutional sites, instructional material. The insider-threat question did they look up how to do this lands here when the method is not itself tooling.

core.name: Entertainment, Streaming & Gaming
core.question: How much of this history is leisure consumption, and when did it happen?
core.boundary: Video and audio streaming, music, film and TV, humour, celebrity, comics and animation, sport as spectacle, and games and gaming platforms.

core.name: Technology, Software & Developer resources
core.question: Was the subject working, or acquiring capability?
core.boundary: Vendor and product documentation, developer platforms, package and code hosting, IT, SaaS and admin consoles, consumer-tech media, AI services. Its primary forensic job is defensive: it keeps ordinary technical work out of the ads and infrastructure label.

core.name: Shopping & Marketplace
core.question: What was purchased, and does it match the alleged fraud?
core.boundary: Retail, auctions, classifieds, marketplaces, coupons, and property listings.

core.name: Finance & Banking
core.question: Which financial institutions and accounts were accessed, and when?
core.boundary: Retail and commercial banking, payments, brokerage, insurance, tax and government financial portals, accounting.

core.name: Cryptocurrency & Exchanges
core.question: Was there an exfil-monetisation or ransom-payment channel?
core.boundary: Exchanges, wallets, chain explorers, mining and token services. Kept separate from Finance & Banking deliberately.

core.name: Employment & Job seeking
core.question: Was there job-seeking before the exfil?
core.boundary: Job boards, applicant portals, recruiter services, CV tooling.

core.name: Travel, Transport & Accommodation
core.question: Does the browsing corroborate the movement timeline?
core.boundary: Booking, carriers, accommodation, maps and routing, local transport. Placement and alibi.

core.name: Health & Medical
core.question: Is there a medical explanation, a capacity question, or a welfare concern?
core.boundary: Conditions, symptoms, providers, appointments, pharmacy in its ordinary sense, mental-health services. Recreational-drug material is not here.

core.name: Adult & Sexual content
core.question: Was there adult material on this machine?
core.boundary: Explicitly not a CSAM detector. Does not extend to dating, sex education, or non-sexual nudity in a medical or artistic context.

core.name: Gambling
core.question: Was there gambling activity?
core.boundary: Betting, casino, lottery, and in-game wagering. Motive evidence in embezzlement and fraud.

core.name: File sharing, Cloud storage & Transfer
core.question: How did the data leave?
core.boundary: Consumer and enterprise cloud storage, document collaboration, large-file transfer, peer-to-peer, paste and snippet services.

core.name: Anonymity & Privacy tooling
core.question: Was there counter-forensic preparation?
core.boundary: VPN, Tor and proxy services, encrypted-DNS and DNS-tunnelling services, anonymous mail and disposable identity, secure-delete and anti-forensic tooling, remote-desktop services used for access concealment.

core.name: Hacking & Security tooling
core.question: Was there tool acquisition or capability building?
core.boundary: Offensive tooling, exploit and vulnerability material, credential and password-attack resources, malware analysis and reverse-engineering resources, hacking community material. Distinguished from Technology by offensive or intrusion-oriented purpose, not by technical difficulty.

core.name: Ads, Trackers & Web infrastructure
core.question: Which of these rows record an act by the user at all?
core.boundary: Advertising and tracking beacons, CDN and asset hosts, URL shorteners and redirect hops, parked and for-sale domains, login and consent walls, private-IP and appliance hosts, browser-internal pages. A positive identification that the row is machine-originated or content-free.

core.name: Unclassified / insufficient signal
core.question: Can this row support any claim?
core.boundary: The row's title and URL together carry no discriminating signal: empty or generic app-shell titles, opaque identifiers, bare hosts with no readable token. A forensic classifier must be permitted to say nothing.
